entities.summary:
The 2020 Zagreb earthquake was a significant seismic event that occurred in Croatia on March 22, 2020. It had a magnitude of 5.3 and lasted for approximately 10 seconds. The earthquake was felt across the country, causing widespread damage and power outages in the capital city of Zagreb. The epicenter of the earthquake was located in the Banovina region, approximately 7 kilometers southeast of Zagreb. The earthquake resulted in the deaths of 5 people and injured over 20. The disaster also caused significant economic losses, with estimates suggesting that the damage exceeded $1 billion. The 2020 Zagreb earthquake highlighted the need for improved earthquake preparedness and emergency response measures in Croatia. The event also led to increased awareness and education about earthquake safety among the general public. The impact of the earthquake was felt for months after the event, with many residents still recovering from the disaster. As one resident noted, 'The earthquake was a wake-up call for us to take earthquake safety seriously and to invest in more robust infrastructure.'

The 2020 Zagreb earthquake resulted in significant changes to the country's disaster management policies and infrastructure. The event led to the implementation of new building codes and safety regulations, aimed at reducing the risk of damage and loss of life in future earthquakes. The Croatian government also invested in the development of early warning systems and emergency response protocols. The impact of the earthquake was not limited to the immediate area, as it also led to increased awareness and education about earthquake safety among the general public. As one expert noted, 'The 2020 Zagreb earthquake was a significant event that highlighted the need for improved earthquake preparedness and emergency response measures in Croatia.'
